definitions.explanation: The act of coming onto land from the sea or from a ship. Also used for typhoons making landfall.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{上陸|じょうりく}した。
{兵士|へいし}たちは{夜明|よあ}けに{海岸|かいがん}に{上陸|じょうりく}した。
examples.english: The soldiers landed on the beach at dawn.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}の{台風|たいふう}が{九州|きゅうしゅう}に{上陸|じょうりく}する{見込|みこ}みで、{各地|かくち}で{警戒|けいかい}が{強|つよ}まっている。
examples.english: A large typhoon is expected to make landfall in Kyushu, and warnings are being heightened across the region.

notes:
Composed of {上|じょう} (up, onto) + {陸|りく} (land). Most commonly encountered in weather reports about typhoons making landfall and in historical or military contexts about troop landings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {台風|たいふう}が{上陸|じょうりく}する (a typhoon makes landfall)
- {海岸|かいがん}に{上陸|じょうりく}する (land on a coast)
- {島|しま}に{上陸|じょうりく}する (land on an island)
- {上陸|じょうりく}{地点|ちてん} (landing point)
- {上陸|じょうりく}{作戦|さくせん} (landing operation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {着陸|ちゃくりく} — landing (of an aircraft, not from sea)
- {入港|にゅうこう} — entering port (ship arriving at harbor)
- {下船|げせん} — disembarkation (getting off a ship)
